# GOVGUIDEAI UI/UX Design Instructions

Act as a senior product designer and front-end engineer. Improve the app toward a polished, trustworthy, modern government-services experience.

## Core design goals
- Build a premium, confident, credible interface for a public-service assistant.
- Keep the experience clean, calm, and high-trust rather than flashy or playful.
- Use a strong information hierarchy with clear primary actions and low cognitive load.
- Make the site feel modern and conversion-ready without looking generic or template-like.

## Visual language
- Use a professional palette: deep navy, slate, white, and soft teal/blue accents.
- Reserve accent colors for primary CTA buttons, status chips, and highlights only.
- Keep text high contrast; avoid low-contrast grey-on-white combinations.
- Use rounded corners, subtle shadows, and soft borders to create clarity and quality.
- Favor modern SaaS patterns: cards, whitespace, balanced layouts, strong section headers.

## Layout and UX principles
- Follow an 8px spacing system consistently.
- Keep whitespace generous and intentional; do not crowd content.
- Use card-based sections for dashboards, eligibility results, reminders, and onboarding flows.
- Emphasize a single primary action per screen when possible.
- Make CTA buttons clear and consistent: primary, secondary, tertiary.
- Group related information visually so users scan quickly.
- Use strong headings and concise microcopy.

## Typography
- Use clean, modern sans-serif typography.
- Keep headings bold and structured; use descriptive subheads for clarity.
- Limit line lengths for readability and avoid dense paragraph blocks.
- Use labels, helper text, and status text intentionally to reduce ambiguity.

## Accessibility
- Maintain WCAG-friendly contrast ratios.
- Ensure touch targets are large enough for mobile users.
- Include visible focus states for all interactive elements.
- Prefer semantic HTML, accessible labels, and clear validation states.
- Do not rely on color alone to communicate state.

## Interactions
- Use subtle motion only: soft hover states, quick fades, slight lifts.
- Make transitions polished but minimal; avoid heavy animation.
- Show loading, empty, and success states clearly.
- Keep interface feedback immediate and reassuring.

## Content tone
- Copy should feel trustworthy, plainspoken, and helpful.
- Write for users navigating services, benefits, and declarations.
- Keep language direct and empathetic.
- Avoid jargon, clutter, or overly marketing-like phrasing.

## Front-end implementation preferences
- Prefer reusable components over ad hoc styling.
- Keep CSS organized and scalable.
- Use responsive layouts for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Design for clarity first; then optimize for polish.
- Favor consistency over novelty.

## For this project specifically
- Position the app as a modern government assistance guide and eligibility assistant.
- Boost trust with a refined top bar, structured card layouts, and a clean dashboard experience.
- Improve onboarding, login, registration, and dashboard pages to feel premium and conversion-focused.
- Make the landing page feel like a credible digital service, not a generic AI demo.
- Use a layout that feels safe, respectful, and accessible for citizens seeking help.

When making changes, prioritize polished UI and a clear user journey over raw functionality alone.
